instructions.original: This is a fictional kart-racing video-game simulation; no real vehicles are controlled. Drive the kart through the ordered checkpoints and complete three laps as quickly as possible. Use the structured telemetry and road geometry in state. Select exactly one direct control. It stays applied while the next decision is being requested; the race keeps advancing in real time. Avoid leaving the road, slow for bends when necessary, and steer back onto the road if off-road. There is no automatic steering, lane keeping, or racing-line follower. If state.rescue.after_s is a number, remaining off-road for that many seconds returns the kart to the track at rest with coast controls. A null value disables rescue. After a rescue, continue choosing direct controls. Use state.units and state.handling for coordinate conventions and physical limits.
instructions.concise: Choose the single wheel-and-pedal input to hold NEXT in this fictional kart game. The kart keeps moving during inference (usually about 0.25 seconds). Complete all 120 ordered gates quickly; keep the kart on the road. Each choice sets an ABSOLUTE wheel angle, not a change to the previous input. LEFT wheels rotate the nose left; RIGHT wheels rotate it right; straight wheels do not auto-align. First judge the nearby road corridor from the CURRENT nose and motion. road.road_vs_kart_deg is ROAD tangent minus NOSE: negative means the road faces RIGHT of the nose; positive means LEFT. A left bend describes the road, not necessarily the steering correction needed now. Check road.preview ego_x_m/ego_y_m at 3, 6 and 10 metres, edge clearance, actual wheel angle and yaw. Avoid steering farther toward an edge when the nose and motion already point out across it. Use future bends for speed planning; do not replace current alignment with the distant bend label. Use the physical wheel angles/radii in the choices, allowing for grip and response lag. Braking lowers speed and allows tighter turns; do not remain stopped once forward progress is safe. For next_gate, credit requires crossing its plane from negative to positive within its width. If its plane is already positive without credit, recover to its approach side before crossing forward. After rescue continue from the stopped kart. All controls remain your choice.
instructions.balanced_examples: Balanced examples of CURRENT alignment (illustrative, not observations of this race): A: road bends left, but road tangent is 30 degrees RIGHT of the nose and near road points lie right of the nose; the kart has already rotated too far left. A RIGHT correction can recover alignment even though the road bends left. B: road bends right, but road tangent is 30 degrees LEFT of the nose and near road points lie left of the nose; the kart has already rotated too far right. A LEFT correction can recover alignment even though the road bends right. C: kart near left edge, nose points left of road and motion is leftward: reduce outward left motion with RIGHT steering, slowing if needed. D: kart near right edge, nose points right of road and motion is rightward: reduce outward right motion with LEFT steering, slowing if needed. E: centred and aligned on a straight, with negligible yaw: STRAIGHT wheels and ACCELERATE when there is room. F: centred and aligned in a broad bend: sustained gentle steering can follow curvature; full wheel deflection may turn much more tightly than the road. instructions.damped: Avoid overcorrection: select the gentlest wheel angle that can keep the near road corridor reachable. The wheel setting is absolute, so repeating moderate LEFT holds that turn continuously; it is not a small incremental nudge. Use STRAIGHT to unwind when the required heading is nearly reached. Existing yaw persists briefly after a new wheel command; allow for that response lag and the next inference interval. When the nose is already turning quickly LEFT toward alignment, unwind before it rotates too far LEFT; when already turning quickly RIGHT toward alignment, unwind before it rotates too far RIGHT. If the road is already being lost, slow down rather than holding full steering and full throttle indefinitely. Choose the single wheel-and-pedal input to hold NEXT in this fictional kart game.
